newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Prayers to mark anniversary of Port Arthur massacre.
newsitem.headline: Prayers to mark anniversary of Port Arthur massacre.

text.p: The 35 victims of Australia's Port Arthur massacre will be remembered on Monday, the first anniversary, in a church service to be held among convict ruins where the killings took place.

Hundreds of people whose lives were forever altered by the shootings, including family of the dead and survivors, are to join in prayer with dignatories from around the country in a nationally televised memorial service.
The morning service will be held inside the stone ruins of the Port Arthur church, now without a roof and carpeted with grass.
On April 28 last year, within a stroll from the church, a young gunman shouldered a semi-automatic rifle and, for no apparent reason, unleashed modern Australia's worst mass murder.
By the end of that afternoon, 35 people lay dead in and around the former penal colony of Port Arthur, a busy tourist attraction on the island state of Tasmania.
Gunman Martin Bryant, 29, a loner with a grudge against society, is now serving life imprisonment without parole after pleading guilty to what prosecutors called senseless slaughter.
He refuses to say what motivated him and, although he will spend Monday caged alone in his suicide-proof cell in the state capital Hobart, Bryant will haunt the anniversary.

"The recovery process would have been expedited if capital punishment had been exercised," Craig Coombs, chief executive of the Port Arthur Historic Site, said, expressing the feelings of many touched by the tragedy.
People around Australia have been asked to light candles on Monday in memory of the dead in a gesture similar to that paid last month to the 16 young victims of Britain's Dunblane massacre.
On March 13 last year, barely a month before the Port Arthur killings, Thomas Hamilton fired on grade-one pupils in a school in the Scottish town of Dunblane before shooting himself dead.
The massacres prompted British and Australian authorities to crack down on firearms. In Australia for the first time, rapid-fire weapons were outlawed in every state and territory.
Memorial church services to mark the first anniversary of the Port Arthur killings will also be held on Monday morning in other major cities across the country.
